source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

This is precisely the study I had wanted to see. Thank you for continuing to work through it with me. Once height became the isolated variable, I could finally judge what I had been visualizing.

I’d like the 2% increase to become our new baseline. It gives the Hero V exactly enough quiet elevation without feeling exaggerated.

Before proceeding, however, I noticed several details that appear to have been unintentionally unlocked during this exercise. I’d like to reinstate these previously established design rules.

1. The É accent must be an exact copy of the Hero V’s right arm terminal.

It should not receive a separate interpretation. The Hero V is still the master geometry, and the accent must directly inherit that identical form.

2. The highest point of the É accent must end at exactly the same height as the Hero V’s right arm.

This alignment is now an essential part of the visual language, so those elements should match perfectly in height.

3. The second V needs to remain significantly more restrained.

It should certainly share the same design language, but in a far quieter way. Its percentage increase must be derived from the second V’s original height rather than adjusted visually to resemble the Hero V. Its right arm should rise proportionally above the alphabet while remaining nearly invisible to the eye. At present, it has grown too expressive. It must never challenge the Hero V; it should only echo it.
For the next study, adding three guides would be especially helpful:

Keep the current reference line that indicates the calibrated increase from the original baseline.
Add a guide through the Hero V right arm’s peak so I can immediately confirm that the É accent aligns exactly with it.
Add a guide at the cap height of the remaining alphabet so we can accurately adjust how far the second V rises above those letters.

We are no longer looking for new concepts. We are fine-tuning the relationships among the three signature features that define the identity. They will become the kind of detail that people recognize instinctively without consciously observing it.

Thank you again. I truly feel that we are nearly there.

value_updates.endpoint_elevation: The Hero V right endpoint is 2% higher than the original Option B baseline.
value_updates.terminal_style: the original Option B terminal shape, slope, taper, and profile
value_updates.master_geometry_role: The Hero V remains the master geometry for the signature system.
